AI does the legwork. You make the decisions.

Research and drafts are generated from public web sources, so they should always be checked before use. Tandem Reach is designed around that reality.

  • You approve every message. Drafts stay drafts until you send them.
  • Reasoning is visible. Each match shows why it was recommended.
  • Sources stay traceable. Findings point back to where they came from.
  • Edit anything. Wording, tone and offer are always yours to change.

Questions, answered

What people usually want to know before they try it.

What is Tandem Reach, in plain terms?

Tandem Reach is a workspace for growing through partners. You describe the kind of company you would like to work with, and the AI builds a ranked shortlist, writes a short research brief on each candidate, and drafts a first message you can edit and send.

After that, it helps you keep track of every conversation in one pipeline, so promising leads do not get lost between the first email and a signed agreement.

How does it find the right partners?

It starts from the profile you give it: what you sell, who you sell to, the regions you care about and the type of partner that would help. It then looks across public information about companies, such as their websites, service pages and announcements, and compares what it finds with your profile.

Each company that comes back is placed on the shortlist with a fit score and the reasons behind it, so you can quickly see why it was suggested and decide whether it deserves your time.

Does the AI contact partners without my approval?

No. Everything the AI writes is a draft until you decide otherwise. It never sends a message, books a meeting or replies on your behalf unless you review it and choose to send it.

You can rewrite a draft completely, change the tone, shorten it, or discard it. The drafts are meant to save you the blank-page problem, not to take the decision away from you.

Where does the research come from, and how reliable is it?

The research is generated from publicly available web sources. That keeps it traceable, but public information can be incomplete, out of date or occasionally wrong, and an AI can misread what it finds.

For that reason, treat every brief as a well-organised starting point rather than a verified fact sheet. Before you contact a partner, check the details that matter most, such as what they actually sell, who they serve and any names you plan to mention.

How is the fit score decided?

The score reflects how closely a company matches the profile you defined. It looks at things like the products or services they offer, the customers they serve, their region and how well their business complements yours rather than competing with it.

The score is a guide for prioritising, not a verdict. Open the reasoning behind any number to see what pushed it up or down, and use your own judgement for relationships the data cannot capture.

Who is Tandem Reach built for?

It is designed for teams that grow through other companies: software vendors looking for resellers or integration partners, service firms building referral relationships, and channel or alliance managers who spend too much time on manual research.

It works well for small teams that have no dedicated partnerships staff, and for larger teams that want a more consistent way to find and approach new partners.

What do I need to provide to get started?

Very little. You will be asked to describe your product or service, the customers you serve, the regions you are interested in, and the kind of partner you hope to find. Examples of past partnerships you were happy with also help.

  • A short description of what you sell
  • Your ideal partner type and region
  • Anything that should rule a company out

You can refine the profile at any time, and the shortlist updates to match.

Will it replace my partnerships team?

No. It takes over the repetitive work, such as searching, summarising and drafting first messages, so your team can spend its time on conversations, negotiation and relationships, which are the parts that actually close deals.

Think of it as a research assistant that prepares the groundwork. The judgement, the relationships and the final decisions stay with your people.
